bodyText:
DoSAT 1.0

A Decision Procedure for Do Calculus.

Decide causal satisfiability or whether premises entail a conclusion.

The model class is a supplied acyclic graph of observed Boolean variables with independent private disturbances. Interventions share the same causal mechanisms, so the do-calculus rules apply wherever their conditional terms are defined.

Causal graph

One edge or isolated variable per declaration; semicolons or newlines separate declarations. Up to six Boolean variables.

Premises / constraints

One constraint per line. Empty premises are allowed. Use Pr(Y | do(X)) to set X true, Pr(Y | do(~X)) to set it false, or Pr(Y | do(X), Z) to observe Z after intervention. Simultaneous interventions use do(X, ~Z). Numeric assignments such as do(X=1) remain supported.

Conclusion (entailment only)

One constraint, including arithmetic and logical combinations. A conditional at zero evidence mass is undefined. Countermodels include cases where required undefined terms prevent the conclusion from holding.

 Require strictly positive observational mechanisms

Every observational row then has positive probability. Interventions can still force some rows to have probability zero.

Search mode
Decision procedure (no time limit)
Search with a time limit

Decision mode has no overall time limit. Each stage first tries a QF_NRA strategy with a budget of up to 60 seconds, then uses the complete NLSat procedure if needed. Finite resources can still prevent an answer. A time limit stops accepting results at the requested deadline; cancellation and cleanup can take longer to settle.
